newsitem.title: USA: US corp bonds trade higher, Time Warner debt tight.
newsitem.headline: US corp bonds trade higher, Time Warner debt tight.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were trading up in line with U.S. Treasuries in quiet dealings, traders said.
"Trading was very quiet in both retail and the street," one high-grade trader.
Dealers said spreads to U.S. Treasuries were mostly unchanged, however, Time Warner debt tightened by two basis points.
"Time Warner was tighter by two basis points," said one high-grade trader.
Meanwhile, the corporate primary sector continues to bustle with activity as new debt supply quickly gets scooped up by investors, dealers said.
On Wednesday, Union Carbide priced $200 million in 100-year debentures to yield 7.861 percent, or 97 basis points over Treasuries.
Dealers said the issue was priced right and well received by the market.
"Union Carbide's deal went very well...it's now issue-bid on the street," said one syndicate source.
In addition, Airtouch Communications priced $250 million in seven-year notes to yield 7.019 percent, or 54 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Among other successful deals, Argentina priced $1.0 billion in 10-year global debt to yield a spread of 445 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The size of the deal was boosted from an initial size of $750 million to meet overwhelming investor demand, dealers said.
"Argentina's deal was very successful...it was a blowout," one syndicate source.
Among high-yield new issues, Unisys Corp's new eight-year issue was quoted 101 bid, 101-1/2 offer, traders said.
Loewen's Group's seven-year issue was trading at a spread of 173 basis points while the five-year was bid at 132 basis points, traders said.

In other secondary trading, the wireless sector experienced some volatility following news that AT&T Corp would roll out its digital PCS sevices next year, just as AT&T introduced new PCS-like wireless services on Wednesday, traders said.
Nextel and Vanguard paper were among those that traded off after the news, they added.
"Nextels traded off as much as two points but were currently trading off 1-1/2 points at 63-1/2 bid," one trader said.
